model.title: European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund: simplification and transposition of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies

summary.lead: Official summary (Legislative Observatory, Legislative proposal published):

blocks.label: PURPOSE:
blocks.text: to adopt more suitable and simpler support measures within the framework of the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) and to integrate the necessary changes to ensure the full implementation in Union law of the World Trade Organization (WTO) agreement on fisheries subsidies.

blocks.label: PROPOSED ACT:
blocks.text: Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council.

blocks.label: ROLE OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT:
blocks.text: the European Parliament decides in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure and on an equal footing with the Council.

blocks.label: BACKGROUND:
blocks.text: the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund , established under Regulation (EU) 2021/1139 (the EMFAF Regulation), allocates resources from the EU budget to support the common fisheries policy (CFP), the Union’s maritime policy and its international commitments on ocean governance.

Despite its strategic importance, the current regulatory framework presents implementation challenges . The mid-term EMFAF evaluation and regular feedback from Member States, stakeholders and Advisory Councils (ACs), indicate that funding opportunities are perceived as limited and insufficiently flexible. Legal uncertainty and complexity have been identified as major barriers to supporting the energy transition, small-scale fishing and generational renewal.
It is therefore necessary to amend the EMFAF Regulation to make it more accessible and easier for Member States and beneficiaries to implement.

The proposal and its objectives are consistent with other Union policies, especially environmental, climate, cohesion, agriculture, social, market and trade policies. The proposal is also consistent with the initiatives set out in the European Ocean Pact.

blocks.label: CONTENT:
blocks.text: this proposal seeks to amend the EMFAF Regulation to make it more accessible and easier for Member States and beneficiaries to implement. The proposal also incorporates the necessary changes to ensure the full implementation in EU law of the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, which was adopted at the WTO’s 12th Ministerial Conference on 17 June 2022, was ratified by the EU on 7 June 2023
and entered into force on 15 September 2025.
The proposal is expected to:

- provide greater legal certainty and facilitate the testing of new technologies by introducing new definitions for “energy transition”, “pilot projects” and “demonstrators”, which should not be treated as ordinary fishing vessels;

- accelerate the energy transition of the EU fishing fleet by making engine replacement and modernisation rules more flexible, with a simplified approval process and methodology for emissions reduction calculation;

- have a positive impact on generational renewal by increasing aid intensity for young fishers and the removal of barriers to support the transfer of ownership of business will have a positive impact on generational renewal;
- introduce a new scheme for temporary cessation of activities in order to alleviate the socioeconomic impact on fishers of significant and unexpected reductions in fishing opportunities;
- grant Member States more budgetary flexibility by raising the ceiling for fleet measures and permanent cessation from 15 % to 30 % of each Member State’s allocation;

- ensure full compliance with the agreement on fisheries subsidies by making any operator or vessel engaged in IUU fishing or high seas activities outside the competence of Regional Fisheries Management Organisations (RFMOs) ineligible for EMFAF support.

This proposal would amend the EU's fisheries and maritime funding rules so that support is easier to access and simpler for national governments and fishers to use. It also updates EU law so that it fully matches an international agreement on fishing subsidies that the World Trade Organization adopted in 2022, which the EU ratified in 2023 and which took effect on 15 September 2025. The European Parliament would decide on the proposal together with the Council, on an equal footing.

The main reason for the change is that the current rules are seen as limiting and hard to follow. Reviews and feedback from Member States, stakeholders and Advisory Councils suggest that legal uncertainty and complexity make it harder to support the move to cleaner energy, small-scale fishing and bringing young people into the sector. The proposal is meant to fit with other EU policies, including those on the environment, climate, regional cohesion, agriculture, social issues, markets and trade, as well as the European Ocean Pact.

To make support easier to use, the proposal introduces clear definitions for "energy transition," "pilot projects" and "demonstrators," and says the last two should not be treated as ordinary fishing vessels. This is intended to give more legal certainty and make it easier to test new technologies. Rules for replacing and modernising engines would be more flexible, with a simpler approval process and a clearer method for calculating emissions reductions.

The proposal also aims to help young fishers take over the trade by raising the level of aid available to them and removing barriers to transferring business ownership. A new scheme would support temporary stops in fishing activity to ease the financial hit when fishing opportunities fall sharply and unexpectedly. Member States would gain more budget flexibility, as the limit for fleet measures and permanent cessation would rise from 15% to 30% of each country's allocation.

Finally, to meet the international agreement, any operator or vessel involved in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, or in high seas activity outside the reach of Regional Fisheries Management Organisations, would no longer be eligible for this EU support.
